name: Scan a QR code framed as the way to RECEIVE money
description: A QR scan combined with a UPI PIN entry is framed as necessary to RECEIVE a payment. Scanning a QR and entering a UPI PIN authorises money to go OUT — it never credits money in. This is the specific QR variant of the receive-vs-pay contradiction, distinct from TL-PAY-001's credential form.

manual_retrieval.notes: Original automated retrieval was HTTP 403 (SRC-018 stays RETRIEVAL_FAILED). NPCI's own snapshot states that scanning a QR plus entering a UPI PIN is for making payments, not receiving them.

source_references.quote: Always remember, you don't need a UPI PIN or OTP to receive money.

explanation.plain: You have been told to scan a QR code and enter your UPI PIN to RECEIVE money. Scanning a QR and entering a PIN always sends money out — it can never bring money in. If receiving is the reason given, this is a trick to make you pay.
explanation.technical: RECEIVE_FRAMING + QR_SCAN_REQUEST (payment-action) combined with UPI_PIN_PROMPT (credential-action). NPCI states the QR+PIN act is a payment, not a receipt; CERT-In states categorically no PIN/OTP is needed to receive.
verification_steps: Open your UPI app directly — incoming payments credit automatically with no scan or PIN.
If a PIN or QR scan is demanded to 'receive', stop: that action would debit your account.

provenance.notes: Originally cited to NPCI (SRC-018), HTTP 403 under automated retrieval (G-02). Manually retrieved 2026-08-15 (MR-EVID-003) and verified as exact NPCI primary under DEC-006 / ADR-0015; corroborated by CERT-In SRC-021.
